title: FTS/LTC/CT/23/00016: Martin Faulds
text:
Decision of the First-tier Tribunal for Scotland (Local Taxation Chamber) under
Section 17 of the First-tier Tribunal for Scotland Local Taxation Chamber Rules
of Procedure 2022 (‘The Procedure Rules) and section 81 of the Local
Government Finance Act 1992 in relation to an Council Tax Finance/ Non List
appeal against a decision of a Local Authority.

Chamber Ref:  FTS/LTC/CT/23/00016

Re:
99 McLaren Crescent, Glasgow, G20 0LD (“the Property”)

Parties:

Martin Faulds, 99 McLaren Crescent, Glasgow, G20 0LD (“the Appellant”)

Glasgow City Council, City Chambers, George Square, Glasgow G2 1DU (“Local
Authority”)

The First-tier Tribunal for Scotland (Local Taxation Chamber) (“the Tribunal”)

Tribunal Member:  Nicola Irvine (Legal Member)

1.      Background

1.1
The Appellant appeals the decision of the Local Authority to find him liable to
pay council tax in respect of the Property and to apply for a Summary Warrant
in respect of that liability.

1.2
In terms of section 81(1) of the Local Government Finance Act 1992, the
Appellant is entitled to appeal to the Tribunal if he is aggrieved by a decision of
a local authority that a dwelling is a chargeable, or that he is liable to pay council
tax in respect of such a dwelling. The Appellant was notified in writing by the
Local Authority that it believed that his grievance was not well founded. The
section 81 conditions have been met.

2.      Documents lodged with the Tribunal.

2.1   Email from the Appellant dated 19 April 2023.
2.2   Email from the Appellant to the Local Authority dated 2 August 2022.
2.3   Email from the Local Authority to the Appellant dated 29 June 2022.
2.4   Written submissions from the Local Authority.
2.5   List of Authorities for the Local Authority.

3.
Consideration of the Appeal

3.1
The parties agreed that a hearing was not required and that the appeal could
be dealt with by written representations. The Tribunal determined that it is
appropriate to dispose of the appeal by written representations in terms of rule
9(3) of the Procedure Rules. The issue before the Tribunal was whether the
Local Authority was entitled to apply for a summary warrant in relation to the
Appellant’s council tax liability and to apply a 10% surcharge.

4.
Findings in fact

4.1
The Appellant was liable to pay council tax in respect of the property from 10
May 2016 to 30 June 2016 and from 11 December 2017 to 22 March 2018.

4.2
The notice of appeal was served on the Local Authority prior to 1 April 2023
and has not been withdrawn or otherwise disposed of.

5.
Decision with reasons

5.1
The Tribunal dismissed the appeal.

5.2
There was no material from the Appellant to suggest that he disputed liability to
pay council tax for the periods 10 May 2016 to 30 June 2016 and 11 December
2017 to 22 March 2018.

5.3
The issue for the Appellant is whether the Local Authority was entitled to apply
for a Summary Warrant and apply a 10% surcharge to the liability.

5.4
The email from the Local Authority to the Appellant dated 29 June 2022 sets
out that the Appellant reached agreement with the Local Authority’s collection
agent in 2019 to pay off his outstanding council tax liability at that time. There
is no material from the Appellant to contradict that. The email from the Local
Authority narrates that further council tax bills were issued to the Appellant on
12 October 2021 and that the sums due were not paid within the required time.
Again, there is no material from the Appellant to contradict that.

5.5
In terms of paragraph 2(2) of Schedule 8 to the Local Government Finance Act
1992, the Local Authority is entitled to apply for a Summary Warrant authorising
recovery of the sum remaining due along with a surcharge of 10%.

6. Right of Appeal

In terms of Section 46 of the Tribunal (Scotland) Act 2014, a party aggrieved by
the decision of the Tribunal may appeal to the Upper Tribunal for Scotland on a
point of law only. Before an appeal can be made to the Upper Tribunal, the party
must first seek permission to appeal from the First-tier Tribunal. That party must
seek permission to appeal within 30 days of the date the decision was sent to
them.

Nicola Irvine
